bullets.title: Blue Wave midterms trigger data center moratorium risk across ~58% of planned US AI buildout
bullets.body: Democrats swept the 2026 midterms (Senate expanding to 55 seats; TX, OH, PA flipped), with all six most-watched governor races going to candidates favoring pauses or moratoria on data centers — representing ~58% of planned U.S. AI buildout. Texas alone accounts for ~18-20% of data center capacity through 2030, with the Batch Zero permitting process now in limbo through mid-January leadership transition. Ohio ballot measures passed restricting data center development, and Pennsylvania's flipped Senate compounds Governor Shapiro's existing executive order limiting new capacity.

bullets.title: Market reads data center headwinds as clearing event, not cycle-ender; AI buildout elongation may ease proof-of-concept fears
bullets.body: Multiple strategists argue the election result is a clearing event rather than a structural break — the AI buildout had already re-rated to reflect shakier fundamentals and political headwinds. Elongating the buildout cycle could actually alleviate fears that AI revenue won't justify capex spending, giving monetization time to catch up with infrastructure. Hyperscalers/neoclouds showed cloud revenue growth nearly tripling QoQ, indicating the steep part of the S-curve remains intact.

bullets.title: S&P 500 +1.4% to 7,674 but VIX surges 15.8% to 17.55; AI/tech names decline while healthcare, renewables rally post-election
bullets.body: The S&P 500 rose 1.4% to 7,674.30 on relief from election uncertainty clearing, but VIX spiked 15.8% to 17.55 reflecting cross-currents. Post-election sector rotation is pronounced: renewable energy names (NXT +13.2%) and medical devices (ENOV +15.9%) rallied sharply, while data center/AI-linked names (LBRT -12.0%) declined. NDX underperformed RTY by the most since July 2024 over the past two sessions.

bullets.title: Technicals: Craig Johnson sees regime shift from 'buy dips' to 'sell rallies'; S&P YE target 7,500
bullets.body: Craig Johnson flags 71.4% of stocks in weekly M.A.C.E. downtrends and 26-week New Highs on a sell signal. The September low at 7,507 sits just 7 points above his 7,500 year-end objective, suggesting limited upside. He favors Energy, Healthcare, and regional banks/insurers (Financials Overweight), while downgrading Transportation and upgrading Utilities to Neutral; selling GE, GLW, HWM, UBER.

bullets.title: Hedgeye: WTI breaks $97 signal level; SPX risk range 7501-7684 with negative gamma; long duration bonds added
bullets.body: Hedgeye flags WTI broke its $97 TRADE Signal Level with accelerating downside momentum (Brent TREND at $99 now in play), prompting reduction of energy ETF exposure to 1%. The USD Index fell -0.5% vs. EUR with gold rallying +2.9%; long-duration bonds (ZROZ, BNDD) were purchased on USD weakness. SPX immediate-term risk range set at 7501-7684; UST 10Y range 4.88-5.06%; VIX in chop bucket above 19.

bullets.title: MS QDS: Hedge fund degrossing ~6%+ cumulative; levered ETFs have ~$28bn equity for sale; prefers RTY upside over NDX
bullets.body: Hedge fund net exposure sits at 47% (6th 3-year percentile) with grosses at 206% after >6% cumulative degrossing. Levered ETFs have ~$28bn of equity for sale; macro systematic forecasted $10bn for sale today and another $10bn next week; retail demand running at half pace vs. earlier in year. QDS favors SPX put spreads and shorter-dated protection; RTY upside cheapest of major indices at 26th 5-year percentile vs. NDX at 83rd.

bullets.title: Rates signal growth deceleration; negative stock-yield correlation has flipped since Oct 8
bullets.body: The negative stock-yield correlation that flipped starting October 8 is being read as a growth deceleration signal — falling inflation and growth together is viewed as the worst scenario for equities, particularly cyclicals. Treasury yields are declining (10Y at ~4.921%, down 2.9bps), and global excess liquidity is falling while the Treasury General Account is rising, worsening liquidity conditions.

bullets.title: Eurozone CPI hits 4.0% cycle high in October on energy; PMIs contracting in France and Germany
bullets.body: Eurozone headline CPI rose to 4.0% y/y in October (energy CPI +20.8% y/y), the highest in the current cycle, while core CPI held at 2.5%. PSC's model projects 4.4% y/y by January, well above ECB's 2% target, with markets pricing at least 2 more ECB hikes over the next 12 months. French Composite and German Service PMIs both weakened, with the CAC massively underperforming on French political/fiscal stress.

bullets.title: ADP October jobs: 86k vs. 67k consensus, but professional services shed 27k for third consecutive month
bullets.body: October ADP payrolls beat at 86k versus 67k street expectations, with gains distributed across small (28k), medium (33k), and large (24k) businesses. However, professional and business services shed 27k jobs for the third consecutive month, raising questions about white-collar hiring health. Wage growth remained flat at 3.2%.

bullets.title: September capital goods imports remain elevated, signaling sustained domestic investment demand
bullets.body: Morgan Stanley's U.S. Data Pulse notes that September capital goods imports continue to reflect strong domestic demand, consistent with sustained investment activity in the U.S. economy — a positive read-through for industrials and capex-sensitive sectors despite broader macro uncertainty.

bullets.title: AMD Q3 beats, guides FY27 >80% revenue growth; data center +97% YoY; capacity now the binding constraint
bullets.body: AMD posted Q3 revenue of $13.38B (+2.1% above consensus) with data center revenue of $8.55B (+97% YoY); Q4 guidance of ~$17B (+4.4% above consensus). FY27 guidance calls for >80% revenue growth (vs. ~75% Street), with server CPU growth >100% and DCAI materially above 100%. MI455X/Helios GPU deployments ramping for multi-GW deployments at frontier labs; MI600 co-design underway. Capacity (wafers, packaging) is now described as the key constraint. 83% of sell-side rates Buy; average PT $654.57.

bullets.title: ANET guides 2027 revenue +38-40% YoY; AI fabrics to double to ~$7B; TAM doubled to $220B
bullets.body: Arista reported FQ3 revenue of $3.658B (+58.5% YoY, +10% vs. consensus) with 49.1% operating margin and guided 2027 revenue growth of 38-40% YoY. AI fabrics revenue expected to double to ~$7B in 2027; Campus targeted at $2B (+60% growth). The company's TAM doubled to $220B+ from $105B, driven by scale-across and emerging scale-up opportunities. 100+ AI customers across 10+ accelerator types. Morgan Stanley raised PT to $230, Overweight.

bullets.title: ALAB Scorpio crosses $1B+ annualized run-rate; Q4 guide of $730-750M far exceeds consensus $659M
bullets.body: Arista Labs (ALAB) Q3 beat consensus by ~$35M in revenue; Q4 guidance of $730-750M (+27% QoQ) vastly exceeded the $659M consensus. Scorpio crossed $1B+ annualized run-rate with a second hyperscaler receiving pre-production X-Series in Q3. Growth vectors for 2027+ include NPO optical (2H27 start), custom silicon (>10 engagements, late 2027), and Orion rack-scale ($100K+ ALAB content per rack, 2027 entry).

bullets.title: SpaceX selects Qualcomm for Starlink Mobile nationwide terrestrial 5G network; tower REITs outperform
bullets.body: SpaceX selected Qualcomm's Dragonwing Cellular Infrastructure platforms (QRU100/QDU100) for Starlink Mobile's U.S. terrestrial 5G network — a multiyear agreement to build tens of thousands of cell sites beginning next year, rivaling major carrier scale. SpaceX had previously been declined by Verizon, T-Mobile, and AT&T. Tower REITs (AMT, CCI, SBAC) outperforming on the news as the deployment scale is expected to leverage existing macro tower infrastructure rather than build new.

bullets.title: Dan Ives: AI cycle in third inning of 8-10 year buildout; every $1 capex generates $5-6 broader tech spend
bullets.body: Wedbush's Dan Ives characterizes the AI infrastructure buildout as being in the third inning of an 8-10 year (possibly 12-14 year) cycle, explicitly rejecting dot-com comparisons given strong balance sheets and earnings support. He estimates every $1 of AI capex generates $5-6 in broader tech spending and flags that fewer than 5% of U.S. companies have strategically implemented AI, representing a significant runway for NVDA, AMD, MU, TSM, PLTR, META, AAPL, CRM, NOW, SNOW.

bullets.title: SOX at 12.16x forward P/E approaching 2022 lows; NVDA at 10x (lowest since 2013); Value outpaced Growth by 10ppt in October
bullets.body: Semiconductor multiples have compressed sharply with the SOX at 12.16x forward P/E approaching 2022 lows and NVDA at 10x — its lowest since 2013. Russell 1000 Value outperformed Growth by 10ppt in October, the widest spread since February 2001. AI stocks now show -30% correlation with long-duration Treasuries and +60% correlation with the S&P 500, while ex-AI stocks trade at ~10% correlation — signaling the trade bifurcation.

bullets.title: Post-midterm financials: capital markets named primary driver; MS/GS cleanest plays; two-year M&A window opens
bullets.body: JPM financials strategist argues the election overhang clearing gives corporates a two-year window for strategic M&A, with banks bid and capital markets becoming the primary sector driver. MS and GS are seen as the cleanest capital markets plays. AI buildout rush is expected to generate an earnings tailwind for capital markets before potential legislation. Consumer finance stocks described as undemanding with policy bias toward affordability supporting spending trends.

bullets.title: Citi card data: October consumer spending declined 2.0% ex-food — first monthly decline since May
bullets.body: Citi credit card data shows October sales (ex-food) declined 2.0% for the month on a 2-year basis, the first monthly decline since May, with the slowdown concentrated in week 4. Biggest year-over-year declines hit Apparel, Footwear, Home Furnishings, Home Improvement, and Sporting Goods, with Food Retail, Auto Parts, and Consumer Electronics also decelerating 200+ bps month-over-month.

bullets.title: Hyperscalers (AMZN, GOOGL, MSFT, META) in talks with environmental groups on responsible data center framework
bullets.body: AMZN, GOOGL, MSFT, and META are in discussions with the Sierra Club and NRDC on a responsible data center development framework — a signal that hyperscalers are moving defensively to manage state-level political headwinds by proactively engaging environmental stakeholders rather than fighting regulation outright.

bullets.title: SPX Q3 EPS growth tracking +30-33% YoY; buyback flows set to accelerate post-earnings into Q1
bullets.body: S&P 500 Q3 EPS growth is tracking +30.6% to +33% YoY across multiple estimates, well above typical beat rates. Buyback flow support is expected to step up meaningfully post-earnings blackout period, with a further acceleration into Q1 after a 12-month operating cash flow surge. Data center construction spending is up 90% YoY to a record $96.5B.
